regions.name: Tequila Valley (Valle de Tequila), Jalisco
regions.geography: Low valley around the town of Tequila; volcanic soils, warmer and drier than the highlands.
regions.distinctions: Agave grows smaller and more herbaceous than highland agave; valley blancos read savory and vegetal in editorial guidance — a cultural description, not a legal boundary.

regions.name: Jalisco highlands (Los Altos / La Alteña), Jalisco
regions.geography: High plateau east of the valley (around Arandas and the La Alteña area); red mineral soils, cooler nights.
regions.distinctions: Highland agave reads sweeter and more floral in editorial guidance; some traditionalists stone-roast. A cultural/agronomic distinction, not a legal class.

regions.name: Valles Centrales, Oaxaca
regions.geography: Valley system around Oaxaca City, including Santiago Matatlán and Tlacolula.
regions.distinctions: Heartland of palenque mezcal; pechuga is a specific distillation tradition here, not a category of its own.

regions.name: Sierra Norte, Oaxaca
regions.geography: High mountains north of the valleys; high-altitude wild agave country.
regions.distinctions: Tobalá grows here and beyond; finding a mature tobalá is a matter of personal pride for a mezcalero — a cultural note, not a legal area.

regions.name: Sierra de Sonora (mountain country), Sonora
regions.geography: Mountain municipalities (Aconchi, Álamos, San Pedro de la Cueva, and neighbors) where bacanora vinatas work.
regions.distinctions: Bacanora's official coverage is municipal within Sonora (since the 2000 DO), never the whole state.

regions.name: Sierra Occidental de Jalisco
regions.geography: Mountain country west of Guadalajara, around La Vieja and the Sierra de Talpa.
regions.distinctions: Sierra raicilla taberna country; the DO declaration names specific municipalities in Jalisco, so no whole-state shading.

regions.name: Costa Sur / Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco
regions.geography: Coastal mountains and canyons of southwestern Jalisco, around Cabo Corrientes.
regions.distinctions: Costa is an editorial tradition split of raicilla, not a legal class.

regions.name: Tuxcacuesco region, southern Jalisco (Jalisco–Colima borderlands)
regions.geography: Southern Jalisco river canyons around Tuxcacuesco and Zapotitlán de Vadillo, reaching toward Colima.
regions.distinctions: Tuxca has no denomination of origin; vinatero practice is cultural, and bottles carry no NOM — that is a legal fact, not an authenticity judgment.

regions.name: Comitán de Domínguez, Chiapas
regions.geography: Highland plateau of central Chiapas around Comitán de Domínguez.
regions.distinctions: Comiteco is a regional tradition without a DO; composition (agave vs cane sugars) is verified per bottle, never assumed.

regions.name: Nanacamilpa and central Tlaxcala
regions.geography: Pulque heartland on the Tlaxcala–State of México highlands.
regions.distinctions: Destilado de pulque is a regional tradition, explicitly not mezcal; fermented pulque itself is not a spirit and stays out of the catalogue.

regions.name: Northern Chihuahuan Sierra, Chihuahua
regions.geography: Sierra and desert country of northern Chihuahua, from the Sierra to Delicias.
regions.distinctions: Sotol's DO (2002) covers Chihuahua, Coahuila and Durango; Dasylirion is not an agave, and the app keeps that explicit.
